public_rationale: GitHub Copilot was a serious candidate: Microsoft reported 1.8 million paid subscribers and practical benefits for named customers. Independent survey evidence nevertheless showed infrequent ChatGPT use among many consumers. Neither record settles the claim. Paid adoption alone does not establish sustained compelling utility, and limited consumer use does not exclude a professional killer app. The visible-pipeline component also remains insufficiently evidenced.
limitations: The survey covers six countries and includes several fieldwork days before the target quarter.
The result depends on an unspecified killer-app threshold and the present-pipeline reading of on the horizon.
Later adoption cannot by itself establish what was available or visibly forthcoming in July 2024.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI has no killer apps, and none are on the horizon.

statement.excerpt: There are no killer apps, and no killer apps on the horizon.

from_speaker: no killer apps on the horizon
our_interpretation: I read killer app in its ordinary sense: an application whose compelling practical value drives substantial, sustained adoption of the technology.
A professional application can qualify; the wording does not require adoption by most consumers.
I read on the horizon as describing credible applications visibly forthcoming at publication, not as a prediction that no such application will ever emerge.

For the ongoing state, I use April 1 through June 30, 2024, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication in which application use could be publicly observed. The speaker supplies no reporting period.
Paid subscriptions, repeat use and demonstrated benefits are relevant indicators. None alone automatically establishes killer-app status.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence across leading available and credibly forthcoming applications shows no application combining compelling utility with substantial sustained adoption, and no demonstrated candidate clearly approaching that status.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one available or credibly forthcoming application demonstrably combines compelling practical value with substantial sustained adoption or strong direct evidence of imminent adoption.

evidence.explanation: Microsoft reported current paid Copilot subscriptions of 1.8 million and identified customers seeing practical benefits.
